newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CONTINUES WEAK IN TIGHT MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CONTINUES WEAK IN TIGHT MARKET.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar opened weaker on the U.S. dollar on Tuesday as import pressure continued unabated on the interbank market with no sign of the central bank coming to the rescue, dealers said.
"It looks like the market is still short from Monday and this is most likely to remain the case until the central Reserve Bank comes in," one dealer said.
"The local dollar could depreciate to 11.4100/4200 by the end of the day if the central bank doesn't intervene," he predicted.

At around 0740 GMT the local currency was trading at 11.4025/4125 on the U.S. dollar compared to late Monday's 11.4000/4000. It firmed against sterling to 19.0600/0800 from 19.0810/1095, responding to a stronger U.S. dollar overseas.
It was at 6.3100/3300 from 6.3510/3575 versus the mark but was weaker on South Africa's rand at 2.5500/5700 compared to 2.4920/4940.
